message.content:
**Answer:** The **Statue of Liberty** (1886) by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi is widely regarded as the most famous sculpture of the 19th century. **Why it’s so iconic** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Date** | 1886 (completed and dedicated) | | **Location** | Liberty Island, New York Harbor, USA | | **Symbolism** | A colossal allegorical figure representing liberty, enlightenment, and freedom; a universal icon of democracy and hope | | **Cultural Impact** | • Gift from France to the United States in 1886
• Became a global symbol of immigration, freedom, and international friendship
• Featured in countless films, books, and artworks | | **Technical Achievement** | • Constructed using a wrought‑iron framework and copper cladding
• Designed to withstand harsh marine weather conditions | **Other notable 19th‑century sculptures** | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | *The Gates of Hell* | Auguste Rodin | 1880–1917 | Monumental bronze work depicting scenes from Dante’s Inferno; a landmark in modern sculpture | | *The Kiss* | Auguste Rodin | 1888–1911 | Celebrated bronze of lovers; a masterpiece of emotional realism | | *The Birth of Venus* | Alexandre Cabanel | 1863 | Classicist painting turned into a celebrated sculpture; epitomizes academic art | | *The Oath of the Horatii* | Jacques-Louis David | 1791 | Though slightly earlier, it remained influential throughout the 19th century | **Bottom line** While many masterpieces were created during the 19th century, the Statue of Liberty stands out as the most universally recognized and celebrated sculpture from that era.
